meta.name: Detect smart meter anomalies and route critical alerts via HTTP API

parameters.content:
## Detect Abnormal Smart Meter Consumption

### How it works

This workflow runs on a schedule or manually, pulls recent readings for a group of smart meters from the metering API, and computes a statistical baseline (mean/std-dev) per meter. It flags spikes, drops, suspected leakage (continuous flow during off-hours), and stuck/faulty meters (near-zero variance despite active load). Anomalies are classified into a fault category and severity, and the flow branches into a critical-escalation path (after a short cool-down/dedup wait) or a standard logging path.

### Setup steps

- Configure the metering API in the HTTP Request node, including meterApiUrl, meterGroupId, and authentication credentials.
- Set thresholds in the config node: spikeZScoreThreshold, dropZScoreThreshold, stuckVarianceThreshold, leakageOffHourStart/End, leakageMinFlowThreshold, criticalScoreThreshold.
- Connect the two output Set nodes ("Prepare Critical Alert Dispatch" and "Prepare Standard Alert Log") to your own ticketing/paging/notification system (e.g. Jira, PagerDuty, Slack, email) — they are left generic on purpose.
- Verify the API response shape matches what the code nodes expect: { meters: [ { meterId, address, readings: [ { timestamp, value }, ... ] } ] }.

### Customization

Adjust the anomaly scoring weights, off-hours window, stuck-meter variance threshold, and severity cutoffs to match real consumption patterns for your meter population.

## Start and configure scan

Provides scheduled and manual entry points, then initializes shared workflow settings such as the metering API URL, meter group, and all detection thresholds.

## Fetch meter readings

Calls the smart meter API for recent readings across the configured meter group, then waits briefly to let the readings batch settle before analysis.

## Analyze and detect

Computes a baseline mean/std-dev per meter, checks for spikes, drops, off-hours leakage flow, and stuck readings, then decides whether an anomaly exists.

## Classify and prioritize

Turns the raw anomaly signals into a fault category (equipment fault, leakage, spike, drop) and a severity level, and builds the alert payload used downstream.

## Critical escalation

Critical-severity anomalies wait through a short cool-down/dedup window before being marked ready for immediate dispatch (e.g. paging, urgent ticket).

## Standard logging

Warning/Info anomalies skip the escalation wait and are marked ready for routine logging or a non-urgent ticket.
